look_here_first: Check leathery evergreen to subevergreen NARROW leaves with a few large teeth (or entire margins), then dark bark peeling in long strips. Confirm a tiny shallow cup with strongly, regularly BUMPY/tuberculate scales; this beats leaf shape by itself.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Evergreen or subevergreen shrub/small tree, commonly on dry limestone slopes and canyons.

key_traits.label: Bark
key_traits.text: Dark brown, furrowed, exfoliating in long strips.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Narrowly lanceolate to oblong, leathery, usually with about 3–5 coarse teeth per side; teeth/lobes mucronate; underside densely stellate-hairy.

key_traits.label: Acorn
key_traits.text: Cup shallow, with strongly and regularly tuberculate scales; nut small, ovoid to oblong/subcylindric.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: FNA mature leaf 20–60(–90) × 10–20 mm; narrowly lanceolate/oblong, often 3–5 coarse mucronate-tipped teeth per side but sometimes entire.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Only 4–6 lateral veins on each side (often branching); lower surface generally densely covered with minute appressed stellate hairs.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Bud very small, about 1–1.5 mm; bark dark brown, furrowed, shedding in strips; twigs initially short-stellate hairy.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Acorn cup shallow, approximately 3–4 mm deep by 10 mm wide; cup scales reddish brown, markedly and evenly tuberculate; nut up to roughly 12 mm.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: An old or shade leaf with an entire margin can resemble a live oak; examine bark, lateral veins, and the mature cup.
